_meta.indication: SAVAYSA is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF; not to be used if CrCL > 95 mL/min), and for treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) following 5 to 10 days of initial parenteral anticoagulant therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-national, double-blind, double-dummy, warfarin-controlled (titrated to INR 2.0 to 3.0) non-inferiority study of two SAVAYSA arms (60 mg and 30 mg); non-inferiority margin 38%.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) with one or more additional risk factors for stroke (e.g., prior stroke/TIA, or 2+ of age ≥75, hypertension, heart failure, or diabetes).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: First stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) or systemic embolic event (SEE) during treatment or within 3 days of last dose.
pivotal_trials.n: 21,105 patients randomized (SAVAYSA 30 mg N=7002, SAVAYSA 60 mg N=7012, warfarin N=7012).
pivotal_trials.result: First stroke or SEE: SAVAYSA 60 mg 182 (1.2%/yr) vs warfarin 232 (1.5%/yr), HR 0.79 (CI 0.63, 0.99), p=0.017; both edoxaban arms non-inferior to warfarin. Superiority of the 60 mg arm was not established (ITT HR 0.87, 99% CI 0.71, 1.07).

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, double-blind, double-dummy, warfarin-controlled (titrated to INR 2.0–3.0), event-driven non-inferiority study of SAVAYSA 60 mg once daily (30 mg for dose-reduction criteria) after at least 5 days of initial heparin.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with acute symptomatic venous thromboembolism (DVT or PE with or without DVT) confirmed by imaging, following at least 5 days of initial parenteral heparin therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Symptomatic recurrent VTE (composite of recurrent DVT, new non-fatal symptomatic PE, and fatal PE) during the 12-month study period.
pivotal_trials.result: Symptomatic recurrent VTE: SAVAYSA 130/4118 (3.2%) vs warfarin 146/4122 (3.5%), HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.70, 1.13); SAVAYSA non-inferior to warfarin.

key_safety: The most serious adverse reactions were bleeding. In NVAF the most common reactions (≥5%) are bleeding and anemia; in DVT/PE the most common (≥1%) are bleeding, rash, abnormal liver function tests and anemia. In ENGAGE, Major Bleeding for SAVAYSA 60 mg was 357 (3.1%/yr) vs warfarin 431 (3.7%/yr), HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.73, 0.97); GI bleeding was higher with edoxaban (205, 1.8%/yr vs 150, 1.3%/yr).
target_moa: Edoxaban is a selective, reversible inhibitor of Factor Xa; inhibition of FXa reduces thrombin generation and thrombus formation.
modality: Small molecule (direct oral Factor Xa inhibitor)

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning: (A) Reduced efficacy in NVAF patients with CrCL > 95 mL/min (increased ischemic stroke vs warfarin); (B) Premature discontinuation of SAVAYSA increases the risk of ischemic events; (C) Spinal/epidural hematoma with neuraxial anesthesia/spinal puncture, which may cause long-term or permanent paralysis.

rems.type: FDA (DRISK and DHP) concurred that a REMS is not required for edoxaban.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the Division of Hematology Products concluded the data did not require ODAC discussion of the risk/benefit of the anticoagulant.

description.text: Labeling update (Sections 6 and 14) adding results from the DU176b-D-U311 study of edoxaban in cancer-associated venous thromboembolism

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for an update in the United States Prescribing Information (USPI) Section 6 Adverse Reactions and Section 14 Clinical Studies with the results from study DU176b-D-U311, entitled, "A Phase 3b, prospective, randomized, open-label, blind evaluator (PROBE) study evaluating the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight (LMW) heparin/edoxaban versus dalteparin in venous thromboembolism associated with cancer." In addition, inclusion of the terms thrombocytopenia, angioedema, hypersensitivity, and urticaria in Subsection 6.2 Postmarketing Experience, and an update in Subsection 7.1 to include selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)/serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs).

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use labeling based on pediatric VTE PK/PD and phase 3 study reports

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to section 8.4 Pediatric Use in the Prescribing Information and the Medication Guide.

summary.text: Standard full approval via a 505(b)(1) NDA received January 8, 2014 (PDUFA goal date January 8, 2015), supported by the ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (NVAF) and Hokusai VTE (DVT/PE) phase 3 trials; approved first cycle with no advisory committee meeting and no REMS, with two chemistry-related postmarketing commitments.

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated January 8, 2014, received January 8, 2014, submitted under section 505(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for SAVAYSA (edoxaban tosylate) 15, 30, and 60 mg Tablets.
The PDUFA goal date is January 8, 2015.
The data submitted for review by the Division of Hematology Products did not require a discussion by ODAC regarding the risk/benefit of this anticoagulant.
